title: Where the four braid, and where they part
lede: Twenty shared beats, top to bottom. The braid pulls tight where the four agree and bulges where they disagree — the bulge is measured divergence, not decoration. A strand fades to a dashed thread where that voice is silent. Read down; click any beat.

spine.beat: female follower(s) travel to the tomb early on the first day
spine.note: MATT names two Marys; MARK three women with spices; LUKE a group with spices; JOHN Mary Magdalene alone

spine.beat: the sealing stone is found/made displaced from the tomb entrance
spine.note: MATT dramatizes an angel rolling it in real time; MARK/LUKE/JOHN find it already moved (divine passive)

spine.beat: the women/witness(es) enter or peer into the tomb
spine.note: MARK and LUKE enter bodily; JOHN has the disciples enter and Mary bend down to look; MATT omits an interior entry

spine.beat: the body of Jesus is discovered absent from its burial place
spine.note: framed as angelic declaration in MATT/MARK/LUKE and as empirical discovery-then-report in JOHN

spine.beat: one or more numinous figures (angel/young man/two men) are present at the tomb
spine.note: MATT one angel outside; MARK one young man inside; LUKE and JOHN two figures; JOHN's appear only in Mary's second visit

spine.beat: the numinous figure(s) are visually marked by whiteness/dazzling appearance
spine.note: lightning/snow (MATT), white robe (MARK), dazzling clothes (LUKE), white (JOHN)

spine.beat: the witnesses react with fear, dread, or bewilderment
spine.note: MATT guards struck down + women's mingled fear/joy; MARK alarm/terror; LUKE terror + bowing; JOHN grief rather than terror

spine.beat: the figure(s) address the witnesses with a speech-act interpreting the empty tomb
spine.note: MATT/MARK a commission; LUKE a rhetorical rebuke + reminder; JOHN only a 'why do you weep' question

spine.beat: the sought one is identified as the crucified Jesus
spine.note: MATT/MARK by the angelic naming, LUKE embedded in the passion-prediction; JOHN never verbalizes crucifixion in this scene

spine.beat: his absence from the tomb is explicitly declared ('he is not here')
spine.note: formulaic in the synoptics; JOHN dramatizes absence but never states the formula

spine.beat: his resurrected/raised status is announced (typically as divine passive)
spine.note: MATT/MARK/LUKE via the figures' proclamation; JOHN gestures at it only through the beloved disciple's belief and a scriptural aside

spine.beat: the witnesses are invited to view/verify the vacated burial spot
spine.note: MATT/MARK by directive ('come, see'); LUKE by finding no body; JOHN by inspection of the linen wrappings

spine.beat: a prior word of Jesus is invoked to frame what has happened
spine.note: MATT/MARK cite his earlier promise about Galilee; LUKE cites the passion-and-resurrection prediction; JOHN cites scripture instead

spine.beat: the witnesses depart from the tomb
spine.note: MATT hasten with fear+joy; MARK flee in terror; LUKE return to the eleven; JOHN Mary runs to Peter, disciples return home

spine.beat: the witnesses are commissioned/moved to report to the (male) disciples
spine.note: explicit commission in MATT/MARK; LUKE self-initiated report; JOHN Mary's spontaneous run to Peter/beloved disciple

spine.beat: the announcement is (or is to be) carried to Peter and the wider disciple circle
spine.note: MARK names Peter in the commission (and shorter ending); LUKE the eleven; JOHN Peter and the beloved disciple; MATT names 'his disciples' without Peter

spine.beat: a promise of future seeing/reunion with the risen Jesus is issued
spine.note: both locate it in Galilee via a 'he goes before you' formula; absent from LUKE and JOHN's tomb scene

spine.beat: male disciple(s) go to the tomb to verify the women's report
spine.note: LUKE Peter alone; JOHN Peter with the beloved disciple in a footrace

spine.beat: the linen burial cloths are seen lying in the tomb
spine.note: LUKE a single mention by Peter; JOHN elaborated as wrappings plus separately rolled head-cloth

spine.beat: a closing cognitive/affective state is left unresolved into full belief
spine.note: MARK women's fearful silence; LUKE Peter's amazement; contrast JOHN's beloved-disciple belief and MATT's commissioned joy

distance_note: design-SB: scale bow-out amplitude by `divergence`; render `omission` as a separate channel (strand drop-out). Add the honest note: the linear 20-beat spine is an interpretive alignment, NOT an objective timeline (a variant-graph/DAG is the rigorous successor).
honest_note: The linear 20-beat spine is an interpretive alignment, not an objective timeline — a variant-graph (DAG) is the rigorous successor. Lane position is a fixed map; the band's width is aggregate divergence (how much the four disagree), not a per-gospel claim — which gospel is the outlier at a given beat is a buildable next step.
